topic.label: Earth Systems
topic.desc: Earth Systems: the coupled atmosphere, ocean, land, ice and biosphere, studied through observation, modeling and geospatial analysis.

concepts: Atmospheric circulation, radiation balance, weather and long-term climate change and its drivers.
Physical, chemical and biological processes of the ocean, including currents, heat uptake and acidification.
Plate tectonics, rocks and minerals, earthquakes, volcanoes and the processes that shape landforms over geologic time.
Movement and storage of water through rivers, groundwater, snow and ice sheets.
Cycling of carbon, nitrogen and water through organisms, soils, oceans and atmosphere.
Satellite, aerial and field observation of Earth mapped and analysed with GIS.
skills: Builds radiative energy balance models of the climate and checks equilibrium temperature against observations.
Computes temperature and precipitation trends from station or reanalysis records and checks significance and homogeneity.
Explains observed change in terms of greenhouse, aerosol and natural forcing and checks claims against assessment literature.
Interprets temperature and salinity profiles to describe currents and water masses and checks density consistency.
Decomposes sea level change into thermal expansion and ice melt contributions and checks the budget closes.
Locates earthquake hypocenters from arrival times and checks residuals and magnitude estimates.
Classifies rocks and minerals from described properties and checks identification against diagnostic tests.
Reconstructs depositional history from rock layers and checks relative ages against superposition and dating.
Models rainfall-runoff response for a watershed and checks simulated discharge against gauge records.
Estimates glacier and ice sheet mass balance from accumulation and melt and checks against remote sensing.
Computes drought indices from precipitation and soil moisture and checks severity classes against historical events.
Builds carbon budgets across reservoirs and fluxes and checks that sources and sinks balance within uncertainty.
Assesses ecosystem response to climate and land change and checks conclusions against field and satellite evidence.
Classifies satellite imagery into land cover classes and checks accuracy against reference samples.
Maps flood, fire, landslide and seismic hazard zones and checks layers against recorded events.
Assesses land use and resource decisions against Earth system limits and checks assumptions with cited data.
